comment: The architecture separates knowledge governance (LIMR) from execution (CDSE) but nothing attests that content executed at runtime is byte-identical to content the LIMR governs. The WHO governance -> national LIMR -> CDSE trust chain is only as strong as this hand-off. Observed instance: a current knowledge-manager implementation indexes content by path reference with no copy and no checksum, so evaluation-time bytes are unattested against install-time content (reported on ohs-foundation/kotlin-fhir-knowledge PR #2, Aug 2026).

public.suggestedRevision: Add Required attributes: the LIMR publishes content with integrity metadata (version + hash); the CDSE verifies loaded logic against that metadata and records executed-content identity in decision audit records. This gives 'preserve fidelity' (glossary, p.2) a mechanical enforcement point.
